column1: # What this tree reads differently from the last release, over the corpus of
# tests/docs_corpus_loads.rs and the same corpus with an unknown key planted at every mapping.
# (ADR-052: a comparison that shows a verdict nobody listed stops the pull request.)
# One rule per line, tab-separated:
#   kind <TAB> where <TAB> last release <TAB> this tree [<TAB> page or file]
# kind:   Eval, Mcp, Trust, Sandbox, Pack, Sequence or Assertions.
# where:  the mapping the unknown key was planted in, as a dotted path with * for a list index and
#         (root) for the root mapping; or as-written for the document itself, which then needs the
#         page or file it is in as a fifth column.
# The two verdicts are loaded or refused.
# The list is exact both ways. A difference with no rule fails the test, and so does a rule that
# matches no difference. A change to a reader that changes a verdict adds its rule here in the same
# pull request, next to the Migration entry in CHANGELOG.md that tells a user what to do.
# The rules hold against one release, named on the `against` line. When the release the test is
# given is another one, the rules are not applied: the changes they list are in that release, or
# were written for one that is gone. The next rule added sets `against` to the current release and
# drops the old rules.
